note: The CLASS-first detection recipe: which generic evaluator(s) a sink kind selects. A sink argument's kind (the same `kind` the models/ catalog stamps -- command-injection, alloc-size, weak-crypto, ...) routes to one or more of a CLOSED set of evaluators. A recipe target is either one evaluator name or a LIST of them: a kind can select several patterns over the one flow (a memory copy is both a `relational` size check and a `missing-guard` control-flow check), each firing its own lead. Adding a catalogued kind that maps to an existing evaluator adds a whole detection category with no engine code; only a genuinely new evaluation primitive needs code. Pure data; no engine coupling -- an engine reads `kind_evaluator[kind]` (a string or list) and dispatches. The evaluators are a documented vocabulary, not data the engine keys on beyond the closed set.

evaluators.reachability: Injection / traversal. An attacker-controlled value reaching the sink argument IS the lead -- the argument carries no length obligation, so taint alone fires. (command/sql/xss/ssrf/path/...)
evaluators.relational: Size / memory. The delivered length must be BOTH attacker-influenced AND unbounded relative to the destination capacity. Either alone is normal (a bounded tainted length; an unbounded constant). No taint -> no lead. A copy dominated by a size-testing branch (a checked copy) is suppressed.
evaluators.presence: Configuration weakness. The CALL ITSELF is the defect regardless of taint (weak crypto, insecure TLS, predictable temp file). Collected per-call and fires even with constant arguments; taint is not consulted.
evaluators.missing-guard: Control-flow anomaly. A validating branch that tests this obligation's variable EXISTS in the enclosing function, but the sink is reached on the fall-through path outside that branch's region. The absent check IS the lead, so this is taint-INDEPENDENT (like presence); attacker-reachability is a separate, stronger corroboration. Distinct from no-guard-at-all, which does not fire: the signal is specifically a guard this site escapes.
evaluators.typestate: Temporal lifecycle ordering. A reusable semantic skeleton carries acquire, release, use, escape, and generation transitions; the graph matcher evaluates compatible paths and object identity to report lifecycle violations such as use-after-release, double-release, leaks, and dangling uses.
